sample_formalizations.name: Self-challenge
sample_formalizations.english: Employ mechanisms to disrupt and adversely affect the system or system component.
sample_formalizations.approach: Structure modeling config state (enabled, target, method, severity). Existential theorem proving that when enabled and severity threshold met, disruption components exist.
sample_formalizations.lean4_snippet:
theorem self_challenge_effective (config : SelfChallengeConfig) (severity : Nat) :
  config.enabled = true ->
  severity >= config.min_severity ->
  exists (component : String) (method : String),
    component = config.target_component /\ method = config.disruption_method :=
by
  intro h_enabled h_severity
  exists config.target_component, config.disruption_method
  simp

sample_formalizations.name: Policy and Procedures
sample_formalizations.english: PII processing and transparency policy/procedures must be aligned with risk management strategy.
sample_formalizations.approach: Structure modeling policy state. Compliance predicate as conjunction. Positive proof via simp on example, negative proof showing incomplete policy fails.
sample_formalizations.lean4_snippet:
def complies_pt1 (policy : PT1_Policy) : Prop :=
  policy.has_pii_processing_policy /\
  policy.has_transparency_procedures /\
  policy.risk_management_aligned

theorem valid_policy_complies : complies_pt1 example_policy := by simp [complies_pt1]
theorem incomplete_policy_fails : not (complies_pt1 incomplete_policy) := by simp [complies_pt1]

sample_formalizations.name: ImageLib Boundary Conditions
sample_formalizations.english: Incorrect boundary conditions in Graphics: ImageLib component affecting Firefox < 148 and Thunderbird.
sample_formalizations.approach: Structure encoding version numbers and boundary check flag. Invariant: vulnerable versions must have boundary checks. Proved for safe config (versions above threshold), disproved for vulnerable config.
sample_formalizations.lean4_snippet:
theorem boundary_condition_invariant (config : ImageLibConfig) : Prop :=
  (config.firefox_version < 148 \/ ...) -> config.has_boundary_checks = true

theorem safe_config_ok : boundary_condition_invariant safe_config := by simp [...]
theorem vulnerable_config_bad : not (boundary_condition_invariant vulnerable_config) := by simp [...]

formalization_patterns.structure: LLM consistently creates Lean4 structures to model control state/config
formalization_patterns.invariant: Core security property expressed as a theorem over the structure
formalization_patterns.sorry_note: 5 of 99 successful compilations use sorry (5.1%) - these compile but have unproven goals. Acceptable for structural formalization; full proofs can be tightened later.
formalization_patterns.positive_negative: Many formalizations include both a compliant example and a violating counterexample

recommendation.rationale: The 99% compile rate is excellent. The single failure was a transient LLM API connection error (not a Lean4 issue). The formalization pattern is consistent across all frameworks (NIST, ATT&CK, CWE, CVE, SPARTA, D3FEND). Adding retry logic for API errors would bring this to 100%. The 5.1% sorry rate is acceptable for structural formalization and can be addressed in a later tightening pass.
suggested_improvements_for_full_run: Add retry-on-API-error (would have prevented the 1 failure)
Consider a sorry-elimination pass after initial formalization
Track sorry count as a secondary quality metric alongside compile rate
